video_title: NBA's Big Relocation Drama: Will Blazers Leave Portland?

quotes.speaker: Yaron Weitzman
quotes.summary_phrase: Tom Dundon's potential relocation of the Portland Trail Blazers
quotes.excerpt: Tom Dundon, new owner of the Portland Trail Blazers, is trying to negotiate an arena deal.

text_blocks.speaker: Mike Vorkunov
text_blocks.text: Have you always wanted your own NBA team in your city? Not in New York, not in LA, not in Minneapolis. Well, guess what? There might be one potentially willing to move in the near future. At least that's the concern right now in Portland, Oregon, where the Portland Trail Blazers and the local government in Portland are in a bit of a stalemate, and the Blazers might just leave the Blazers on the move.

text_blocks.speaker: Yaron Weitzman
text_blocks.text: Tom Dundon, new owner of the Portland Trail Blazers, is trying to negotiate an arena deal to refurbish the Moda Center in Portland, and things are at an impasse. The local government there is trying to reach a deal with him to approve $600 million that would refurbish the arena, ostensibly keep the Blazers in Portland, the city they've been in and played in since 1970.

quotes.speaker: Yaron Weitzman
quotes.summary_phrase: Adam Silver's comments on the Portland Trail Blazers' arena situation
quotes.excerpt: Adam Silver's answer was not a 'yeah, no, everything's going to be okay.'

text_blocks.speaker: Mike Vorkunov
text_blocks.text: Adam Silver, the NBA commissioner, addressed it on his during his board of governors press conference earlier this month, and that's the state of the Portland Trail Blazers and whether they stay or go in Portland. If you haven't been paying attention, Tom Dundon, you may know that name, that's becoming a very familiar name around the league and around sports.

text_blocks.speaker: Yaron Weitzman
text_blocks.text: I think I told you, I think I texted you even, right after he answered the question from Sean Highkin, who covers the Blazers up in Portland, asked Adam Silver about all the back and forth between Dundon and the local officials in Portland. And Silver's answer was not a 'yeah, no, everything's going to be okay.' It was, I forget the exact quote, but basically we haven't made as much progress as I would like.

quotes.speaker: Yaron Weitzman
quotes.summary_phrase: Bill Oram's reporting on the potential Portland Trail Blazers relocation
quotes.excerpt: Bill Oram has been raising the alarm about the fact that the Portland Trail Blazers could potentially leave.

text_blocks.speaker: Mike Vorkunov
text_blocks.text: Our friend Bill Oram has been raising the alarm about the fact that the Portland Trail Blazers could potentially leave. I think that's kind of earned him an unfair reputation as the worrier of Willamette County, but Bill has been saying like this is a real possibility, and I think maybe a lot of people didn't take him seriously.

text_blocks.speaker: Yaron Weitzman
text_blocks.text: I spoke to multiple NBA ownership-level sources this week. Every one had the same take: Dundon is bluffing and simply trying to squeeze as much as he can out of the city of Portland. Or, as one said, 'There's nowhere for him to go.'

quotes.speaker: Yaron Weitzman
quotes.summary_phrase: Adam Silver's statement on the Portland Trail Blazers' future
quotes.excerpt: I spent time with Tom and his partners here in Las Vegas. What we are most focused on.

text_blocks.speaker: Yaron Weitzman
text_blocks.text: I have this Silver quote, so it's here. It's 'I spent time with Tom and his partners here in Las Vegas. What we are most focused on right now at the league office is the deal that we discussed when we were in Portland in March. I was hoping more progress would have been made by now on that agreement. It seems to have gone off track in various ways. I have a colleague working with both sides to ensure the Trail Blazers have a long-term future in Portland, but there are several open issues that still need to be resolved.'

text_blocks.speaker: Mike Vorkunov
text_blocks.text: Which the way I translate that was, 'Yeah, we expected the Blazers to stay in Portland. I want the Blazers to stay in Portland, and Tom Dundon is being a bit of a pain in my pain in my ass.'

quotes.speaker: Mike Vorkunov
quotes.summary_phrase: Potential relocation of the Portland Trail Blazers to Raleigh
quotes.excerpt: The place that off the top of my head jumps out is Raleigh, North Carolina.

text_blocks.speaker: Mike Vorkunov
text_blocks.text: My question has always been, where would they go if they were to leave? And I think the place that off the top of my head jumps out is Raleigh, North Carolina, which is where the Carolina Hurricanes, the the hockey team that Tom Dundon owns, currently reside. Portland is the 23rd largest media market in the country. Raleigh, the list I saw this morning, is number 22.

text_blocks.speaker: Yaron Weitzman
text_blocks.text: I'll go up the road to Seattle. I'll still be the Pacific Northwest team, and that's all good, except that the NBA has to approve that. And NBA owners would rather get an expansion fee of $6-7 billion chopped up six ways, as somebody told me. Even if I did like Tom, I'd like $200 million a lot more than that.

quotes.speaker: Mike Vorkunov
quotes.summary_phrase: Tom Dundon's ownership style and cost-cutting measures
quotes.excerpt: He's fired a lot of people that he's probably pissed off with the Blazers.

text_blocks.speaker: Mike Vorkunov
text_blocks.text: He's done a lot to piss off people in Portland. He's done a lot to piss off people around the NBA. He's done a lot to piss off people with the Blazers. He's fired a lot of people that he's probably pissed off with the Blazers because he's firing people left and right and he's cutting costs left and right.

text_blocks.speaker: Yaron Weitzman
text_blocks.text: He's making Adam Silver's life more complicated in a way that he did not foresee. It's very clear this was not, again, Tom Dundon bought the Portland Trail Blazers. He did not buy an NBA team to bring to another city, and that's how it was sold as, is what we've been told.

quotes.speaker: Mike Vorkunov
quotes.summary_phrase: Kevin Calabro's departure from the Portland Trail Blazers
quotes.excerpt: I saw a Joe Freeman, the Oregonian, report that Kevin Calabro is not coming back either.

text_blocks.speaker: Mike Vorkunov
text_blocks.text: I saw a Joe Freeman, the Oregonian, report that Kevin Calabro is not coming back either. So that's a big loss. And I mean, those those are not just like that's how a lot of people interact with your team, right? How you listen to them on the radio, how you watch games on TV.

text_blocks.speaker: Yaron Weitzman
text_blocks.text: Correct. And that's being upended right away. Like you are up you are upending the fan process of how you watch Blazers games, and maybe that's not losing fans, but it's pissing off fans.

quotes.speaker: Yaron Weitzman
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James' free agency and team movement
quotes.excerpt: This has been the longest we've had a free agent drama in a very long time.

text_blocks.speaker: Mike Vorkunov
text_blocks.text: This has been the longest we've had a free agent drama in a very long time. Like this is our first prolonged, like free agent thing since what, KD in 2016? But he announced on July 4th. Carmelo Anthony took that two-week free agency tour in 2014 before he resigned with the Knicks.

text_blocks.speaker: Yaron Weitzman
text_blocks.text: LeBron on a minimum or mid-level is actually surplus value, right, to put it coldly. And just this is not just because the yeah, LeBron's a huge name and everyone will be paying attention and ESPN, everyone will be like following it no matter what, but there is legitimate this is a legitimate basketball story too.

quotes.speaker: Yaron Weitzman
quotes.summary_phrase: The story behind Joel Embiid's Chick-fil-A order
quotes.excerpt: I wrote the definitive Joel Embiid Chick-fil-A story. Can you talk me through what the order looked like?

text_blocks.speaker: Mike Vorkunov
text_blocks.text: I saw a video, it looks like an old video of Landry Shamet doing an interview, and someone asked him about getting the Joel Embiid Chick-fil-A order. And I immediately stopped myself from watching the whole thing because I said, 'Wait a second, I don't want to hear this from Landry Shamet. I want to hear this from your own.' You wrote the definitive Joel Embiid Chick-fil-A story. Can you talk me through what the Joel Embiid Chick-fil-A order looked like back in the day and how you got to do a ride-along with Landry Shamet?

text_blocks.speaker: Yaron Weitzman
text_blocks.text: I was tipped off to this because I was when I was covering the Sixers then, this is around 2019, 2020. I used to listen to like, you know, the Sixers, there was some Sixers player podcast or something like that, and Landry Shamet was on it and said something about getting Joel Embiid a crazy Chick-fil-A order. And I'll give away this part. I was tipped off to this because I was when I was covering the Sixers then, this is around 2019, 2020.

quotes.speaker: Yaron Weitzman
quotes.summary_phrase: Details of Joel Embiid's Chick-fil-A order
quotes.excerpt: It's four chicken sandwiches, four milkshakes, four fries, four sodas, I believe.

text_blocks.speaker: Yaron Weitzman
text_blocks.text: He reads off the order, the basic order, on one phone, and then I believe he has a second phone, I think I'm pretty sure he had a second cell phone, reads off and he goes, and a separate order, this is the key part, a separate order, this needs to be in a separate bag, for chicken sandwiches, four milkshakes, four fries, four sodas, I believe we can confirm if I got that order right, but it's four four, it's like Moses Malone, 4444.

text_blocks.speaker: Mike Vorkunov
text_blocks.text: 5,680 calories. Is that was that in the story? Put that in there?
